title: From October, some parents can stop National Pension premiums without losing pension credit
summary: Starting October 1, 2026, qualifying National Pension Class 1 parents caring for a child under age one can have their premiums exempted regardless of income, while those months still count as paid for the basic pension. The key catch is that it is not automatic: eligible parents must file a notice, and Class 2 employees plus Class 3 dependent spouses use different rules.
why_it_matters: For self-employed, student, unemployed and other Class 1 parents, this can remove a meaningful monthly bill during a baby's first year without creating a gap in future basic-pension credit. The September 3 Japan Pension Service bulletin is a timely reminder because filing opens when the scheme starts on October 1.

claims.text: Japan's National Pension childcare-premium exemption starts October 1, 2026, and the Japan Pension Service's September 3 bulletin again highlighted the launch.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service official bulletin and scheme page

claims.text: Eligible people are National Pension Class 1 insured parents raising a child under age one; there is no income test, the parent-child relationship must continue, and the parent and child must share the same address.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service and MHLW scheme descriptions

claims.text: Class 2 employees and public servants are not covered by this Class 1 scheme, and Class 3 dependent spouses are also excluded.

For a biological mother with maternity exemption, the childcare exemption normally follows that period for up to nine months; for a biological father or adoptive parent, it can run from the month childcare begins through the month before the child's first birthday, up to 12 months.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service and MHLW duration rules

claims.text: Exempt childcare months are treated as if the premium had been paid when calculating the basic old-age pension, and even already-paid or other approved exemption months can be converted to childcare-exemption treatment, with paid premiums credited or refunded.
The standard National Pension premium is ¥17,920 per month in fiscal 2026.
claims.basis: Japan Pension Service current premium table

claims.text: The exemption requires a filing. Saku City states that smartphone electronic filing is available and that paper filing generally requires evidence of the pension number and a maternal-and-child health handbook or equivalent.
claims.basis: Municipal official filing guidance linked to the national scheme

claims.text: Because the scheme is not automatic, eligible Class 1 parents who assume childbirth or municipal registration alone triggers the exemption risk continuing to pay premiums unnecessarily until they file.
claims.basis: Inference from the explicit filing requirement

content.key_message: If you are a National Pension Class 1 parent with a child under one on or after October 1, check this exemption and file it—qualifying months can become premium-free without reducing your basic-pension credit.
content.who_is_affected: National Pension Class 1 insured people age 20 to under 60 who are biological or adoptive parents caring for a qualifying child under age one and living at the same address as the child. This commonly includes self-employed people, farmers, students and unemployed people. Class 2 employees/public servants and Class 3 dependent spouses can ignore this specific scheme because different pension rules apply to them.
content.when: The scheme takes effect October 1, 2026. Only October 2026 and later premium months can be covered. A child already born before October can still create eligible months if the child is still under one when the scheme begins.
content.financial_impact: The standard Class 1 premium is ¥17,920 per month in fiscal 2026. Therefore every qualifying October 2026-March 2027 month avoids that month's standard premium while preserving full basic-pension credit for the exempt month. The exact total depends on birth/adoption timing and the premium applicable in each fiscal year.
content.risk_if_ignored: The main loss is paying National Pension premiums for months that could have been covered by the childcare exemption, or leaving the wrong exemption category on the record. Do not assume the municipality or hospital files this automatically for you.
content.deadline: Filing begins with the scheme on October 1, 2026. Prepare before then if you expect to be eligible; after October 1, file promptly through the official channel available for your municipality.
content.effort: Low. Eligibility checking and electronic filing should be a short administrative task if your pension and child information are already registered correctly.
content.potential_benefit: Premium-free qualifying months that still count as paid months toward the basic old-age pension. If both parents are Class 1 and each meets the conditions, both can qualify.
content.downside: This is not a cash grant and it does not apply to everyone with a baby. Class 2 and Class 3 parents are outside this specific scheme, and shared-address plus qualifying parent-child relationship requirements matter.
content.what_would_change_mind: A Japan Pension Service procedural update changing the October 1 filing start, required evidence, electronic-filing availability, or eligibility conditions would require an update. The core entitlement would also need revision if MHLW changes the implementing rules.
content.skeptical_view: The headline benefit can sound broader than it is. This is specifically a National Pension Class 1 exemption, not a universal payment to all parents, and a biological mother's new childcare exemption is generally layered after the existing maternity exemption rather than simply adding 12 more months. Household savings therefore vary significantly by insurance category and timing.
content.what_to_watch: Watch Japan Pension Service and your municipality for the final filing form/interface and any municipality-specific submission notes as October 1 approaches.

30 sec.what_happened: Japan starts a new National Pension childcare exemption on October 1 for qualifying Class 1 parents with children under one.
30 sec.why_it_matters: Qualifying months become premium-free but still count as fully paid months for the basic pension.
30 sec.what_to_do_watch: Confirm that you are Class 1, check the child's age and shared-address condition, then file from October 1 rather than assuming it happens automatically.
30 sec.bottom_line: For eligible parents, this is a real recurring bill reduction with no basic-pension-credit penalty.

reading_levels.2_min: Japan is filling a gap between employees on pension-premium exemption during childcare leave and people in National Pension Class 1, such as many self-employed, student or unemployed parents. From October 1, a qualifying Class 1 parent caring for a child under one can file for premium exemption regardless of income. The parent and child must have an eligible legal/recognized relationship and live at the same address. The exempt months still count as premium-paid months for the basic old-age pension. For biological mothers, the new childcare period generally follows the existing maternity exemption for up to nine additional months; fathers and adoptive parents can receive up to 12 months from the month childcare begins through the month before the first birthday. It is not automatic, so the practical step is to confirm your pension category now and file through the official channel once the scheme opens October 1.

outcomes: Identify whether this new exemption applies to your pension category.
Explain why an exempt month does not reduce basic-pension credit under this scheme.
Distinguish the mother's post-maternity period from the father's/adoptive parent's maximum period.
learning.background: Japan's public pension system has different insured categories. National Pension Class 1 mainly covers people who are not enrolled in employees' pension insurance and are not Class 3 dependent spouses—such as many self-employed people, students and unemployed people. Until now, Class 1 mothers already had a maternity-period premium exemption, while employee pension systems had their own childcare-leave premium rules. The October 2026 change adds a childcare-period exemption specifically for Class 1 parents.

terms.meaning: A person generally age 20 to under 60 living in Japan who is not covered as an employees' pension participant and is not a Class 3 dependent spouse.
terms.why_it_matters: This new childcare exemption is limited to this category.

terms.meaning: A period in which the normal National Pension premium does not have to be paid.
terms.why_it_matters: Under this childcare scheme, the exempt month is still treated as paid for basic-pension calculation.

how_it_works.title: First confirm your pension category
how_it_works.explanation: The new rule is for Class 1. Employees/public servants in Class 2 and dependent spouses in Class 3 should use the rules for their own category instead.

how_it_works.title: Then identify the eligible childcare months
how_it_works.explanation: For fathers and adoptive parents, the period can start in the month childcare begins and run through the month before the first birthday. For a biological mother who has maternity exemption, the childcare exemption generally follows that maternity period for up to nine months.

how_it_works.title: Filing changes the premium treatment
how_it_works.explanation: Once accepted, qualifying months are exempt from the normal premium but are recorded as paid months for basic-pension benefit calculation. Previously paid qualifying premiums can be credited or refunded.

learning.example: Example: a Class 1 father starts caring for a child born October 1, 2026. If all conditions continue, the childcare period can cover October 2026 through September 2027. The exact yen value follows the National Pension premium for each fiscal-year month, so do not multiply the current ¥17,920 rate across future fiscal years without checking the later rate.
takeaways: It is for qualifying Class 1 parents, not every parent.
The exempt months still count as paid for the basic pension.
You must file; do not assume it is automatic.

action_plan.goal: Get every eligible childcare month correctly recorded as National Pension childcare exemption without unnecessary premium payments.
action_plan.who_should_act: Act if you will be a National Pension Class 1 parent living with a child under age one on or after October 1, 2026. Class 2 employees/public servants and Class 3 dependent spouses can ignore this specific filing and check their own pension/childcare rules instead.
action_plan.deadline: The scheme and filing start October 1, 2026. Prepare now; file from October 1 once your official channel is available.
prepare: Your current pension category and basic pension number or My Number information.
The child's date of birth and confirmation that you and the child share the same address.

If filing on paper, check your municipality's official instructions; municipal guidance may require a document showing your basic pension number and a maternal-and-child health handbook or equivalent evidence.
My Number Card and access to Mynaportal if you plan to use electronic filing and your municipality supports the national electronic route.

steps.action: Check that you are enrolled as a National Pension Class 1 insured person during the months you want exempted.
steps.how: Use your pension records/notice, Nenkin Net, or your municipal National Pension counter if your category is unclear.
needed: Pension record or basic pension number
steps.done_when: You have confirmed you are Class 1 for the relevant month.

steps.step: Check the child and address conditions
steps.action: Confirm the child will be under one during at least one month from October 2026 onward and that the parent-child relationship continues with the same registered address.
steps.how: Compare the child's birth/adoption date with the Japan Pension Service eligibility window and your resident-registration situation.
steps.done_when: You can identify at least one potentially qualifying month.

steps.action: Submit the childcare-exemption notice through the official electronic route or your municipality's National Pension counter.
steps.how: Use Mynaportal if the official electronic option is available to you, or follow your municipality's paper/counter instructions. Do not use unofficial forms or third-party agents for a routine filing.
needed: Any municipality-required evidence for paper filing
steps.done_when: The official system or counter has accepted your filing.

steps.step: Verify the record and refund/credit treatment
steps.action: After processing, confirm qualifying months show the childcare exemption and that any premium already paid for those months is credited or refunded as applicable.
steps.how: Check the official notice or pension record after processing; contact Japan Pension Service or your municipal pension desk if the period is missing.
steps.done_when: The qualifying months are recorded correctly and any overpayment treatment is clear.

mistakes_to_avoid: Assuming the exemption is automatic after registering a birth.
Applying even though you are Class 2 or Class 3 and expecting this specific Class 1 scheme to cover you.
Assuming the mother automatically gets another full 12 months on top of the maternity exemption.
Failing to verify months already paid, which may be eligible for credit or refund after the childcare exemption is recorded.

decision_rules.if: You are Class 1 and have a qualifying child under one with the same address on or after October 1
decision_rules.then: Prepare and file the childcare-exemption notice.

decision_rules.if: Both parents are Class 1 and each meets the conditions
decision_rules.then: Each parent should check and file separately; the scheme can apply to both.

decision_rules.if: You are an employee/public servant in Class 2 or a dependent spouse in Class 3
decision_rules.then: Ignore this specific Class 1 filing and use the pension rules for your category.

decision_rules.if: Your child turns one before October 1, 2026
decision_rules.then: This new exemption does not create eligible months because only October 2026 and later months are covered.

action_plan.follow_up: Re-check Japan Pension Service or your municipality in late September/October for the final form/interface, then verify your pension record after filing.
